source: Built-in generic example; common effect; normal CI; analysis scale; DrugA reference
plain: The network included 10 studies comparing 5 treatments. Effects below compare each treatment with DrugA. DrugB: 0.080 (95% confidence interval −0.073 to 0.233). The interval includes no effect; there is no evidence of a difference, which is not evidence of no difference. This estimate is imprecise: the interval also allows effects in either direction. DrugC: 0.187 (95% confidence interval 0.005 to 0.370). The confidence interval excludes no effect. DrugD: −0.042 (95% confidence interval −0.256 to 0.171). The interval includes no effect; there is no evidence of a difference, which is not evidence of no difference. This estimate is imprecise: the interval also allows effects in either direction. Placebo: 0.250 (95% confidence interval 0.116 to 0.383). The confidence interval excludes no effect. Variation beyond chance might not be important. These results assume consistency of direct and indirect evidence and comparable effect modifiers across comparisons. Rankings do not establish clinical importance or causation.
methods: Contrast-based network meta-analysis used generalised least squares with a common-effect inverse-variance model. Entered effects represent the second treatment minus the first, already on the analysis scale; no arm-count conversion or continuity correction is performed. Complete multi-arm comparisons are grouped by study and correlated contrasts use arm variances; the random-effects covariance adds half the between-study variance to shared contrasts. Invalid or inconsistent multi-arm designs are refused. Effects and 95% confidence limits are displayed on the entered analysis scale. Confidence intervals and two-sided tests use the normal Wald approximation. No Hartung–Knapp adjustment is applied. Heterogeneity is reported as Q with chi-squared tests, the DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance and its square root, and I² with a Higgins–Thompson interval through H. I² is the nonnegative Q-based proportion of excess variation. Q is decomposed into within-design heterogeneity and between-design inconsistency. Prediction intervals are not displayed for the common-effect model. P-scores average pairwise certainty derived from the selected model’s two-sided tests; smaller estimates rank better. P(best) uses 10,000 multivariate-normal draws of the fitted effects with their covariance and a fixed random seed. Analyses were run in allmeta nma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 10 studies, 10 contrasts and 5 treatments. Reference: DrugA. DrugB versus reference: 0.080 (95% CI −0.073 to 0.233); p = 0.3071. DrugC versus reference: 0.187 (95% CI 0.005 to 0.370); p = 0.0441. DrugD versus reference: −0.042 (95% CI −0.256 to 0.171); p = 0.6988. Placebo versus reference: 0.250 (95% CI 0.116 to 0.383); p = 0.0003. Between-study variance τ² = 0.0000; τ = 0.0000. I² = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0% to 70.8%); might not be important (Cochrane Handbook v6.5, §10.10.2). Total: Q = 0.35, df = 6, p = 0.9992. Within designs (heterogeneity): Q = 0.31, df = 2, p = 0.8561. Between designs (inconsistency): Q = 0.04, df = 4, p = 0.9998. Rankings: DrugD, P-score 86.5%, P(best) 62.3%; DrugA, P-score 79.3%, P(best) 31.8%; DrugB, P-score 54.6%, P(best) 5.3%; DrugC, P-score 23.5%, P(best) 0.5%; Placebo, P-score 6.1%, P(best) 0.0%; League comparisons (one direction per pair, row versus column): DrugA versus DrugB: −0.080 (−0.233 to 0.073); DrugA versus DrugC: −0.187 (−0.370 to −0.005); DrugA versus DrugD: 0.042 (−0.171 to 0.256); DrugA versus Placebo: −0.250 (−0.383 to −0.116); DrugB versus DrugC: −0.108 (−0.285 to 0.069); DrugB versus DrugD: 0.122 (−0.109 to 0.353); DrugB versus Placebo: −0.170 (−0.293 to −0.046); DrugC versus DrugD: 0.230 (−0.026 to 0.485); DrugC versus Placebo: −0.062 (−0.232 to 0.108); DrugD versus Placebo: −0.292 (−0.497 to −0.087);
flags: Text uses the completed results at the precision displayed by the page. Confidence intervals alone do not establish clinical importance.
Assess consistency and transitivity before interpreting network estimates or rankings.
references: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, version 6.5, section 10.10.2 (Identifying and measuring heterogeneity).
